[EFFECT] The month of the year has a strong non-monotonic effect on predicted hourly demand. January through March carry notably negative contributions (as low as −0.6 to −0.7 in January), meaning the model pulls demand down significantly in winter. From April onward, contributions turn positive and stay elevated through summer and autumn, with the highest boost visible in September through November (reaching roughly +0.25 to +0.30). December then drops back into negative territory, completing the seasonal cycle.

[IMPORTANCE] With an importance score of 0.118 and a rank of 5 out of 9 features, month of the year has a moderate influence on predicted demand — notable, but less decisive than the top-ranked features like hour of the day or temperature.

[RECOMMENDATION] Plan for significantly higher bike availability and staffing from late spring through autumn, especially September to November, and scale back resources during the winter months — particularly January through March — when the model consistently forecasts suppressed demand.
